transcript.content:
Obedience is the honey that sweetens the tea of domestic order—or so the book says—but, my word, what a bitter draught it turned in my mouth. As I sat there, fingers trembling in the icy grip of duty, every instinct urged me forward: follow through, keep things tidy, make the world safe with routine and obedience. Yet, even the best-kept kitchen harbors knives, doesn’t it? My heart thudded remembering all those moments good women swallow their own voices—until, at last, a quiet, stubborn voice of conscience leaked through the starch and polish. In that instant, warmth rushed through me—a mingling of regret and relief—and I simply could not press that button again. For what use is spotless linoleum if it’s scrubbed with someone else’s pain?
